# Define the tutorial packaging format

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial packaging format: the definition of how a
tutorial is packaged so it can be versioned and tested independently of
Dashboard releases. The format specifies tutorial metadata, pinned image
references, and a validation manifest. It is the shared contract between the
Dashboard tutorial gallery (which launches packaged tutorials) and the
tutorial content (which is packaged and validated per the format).

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata schema: the descriptive information a
  packaged tutorial carries (identity, journey it covers, launch mode).
- Define how pinned images are referenced in a tutorial package, so a
  tutorial always launches against known, tested image versions.
- Define the validation manifest: how a tutorial declares what is validated
  and how testability is achieved independent of the Dashboard release
  cadence.
- Define the versioning model for tutorial packages.
- Demonstrate the format end-to-end on at least one sample tutorial:
  packaging it and running its validation manifest.
- The exact schema, field names, and file layout are implementation
  decisions for the delivering team; this epic fixes the contract, not the
  syntax.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written format specification exists covering tutorial metadata, pinned
  image references, and the validation manifest.
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be versioned independently of
  Dashboard releases.
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be validated by executing its
  validation manifest, demonstrated on at least one sample tutorial.
- The format is reviewed and accepted by the teams that consume it: the
  Dashboard gallery implementers and the tutorial content authors
  (workbench/notebook tutorials and pipeline tutorials).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases.
- Enables HLR-1 and HLR-2 (P0), which is why this epic inherits P0 priority
  despite mapping to a P1 requirement.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into a project

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated,
navigable gallery of getting-started tutorials from which a user launches a
tutorial into their own project with one click. Launching a tutorial opens a
workbench pre-loaded with the tutorial notebook, or imports the tutorial
pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance, according to
the tutorial's launch mode.

## Scope

- Add a tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard console (navigation,
  listing of curated tutorials, tutorial detail view).
- Implement one-click launch into the user's project for the workbench
  launch mode: opening a workbench with the tutorial notebook loaded.
- Implement one-click launch for the pipeline launch mode: importing the
  tutorial pipeline into the project.
- Read tutorial packages per the tutorial packaging format (metadata and
  pinned image references) so launched tutorials use their pinned, tested
  images.
- UI/UX design, feature enablement, and exact placement within the Dashboard
  are implementation decisions for the delivering team.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tutorial gallery is reachable from the Dashboard navigation.
- A user can select a tutorial in the gallery and launch it into their
  project with one click.
- Launching a workbench-mode tutorial opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook loaded, using the pinned image
  references from the tutorial package.
- Launching a pipeline-mode tutorial imports the pipeline into the user's
  project.
- End-to-end: at least one tutorial packaged per the tutorial packaging
  format launches successfully through the gallery against the current
  release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline).

# Author and validate the notebook-based getting-started tutorials

## Description

This epic delivers the curated notebook-based tutorials covering five core
getting-started journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run,
first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is authored as notebook
content, packaged per the tutorial packaging format, and tested against the
current release so it is launchable from the Dashboard tutorial gallery into
a workbench.

## Scope

- Author five tutorials as notebook content:
  1. First workbench — creating and using a first workbench.
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — deploying a first model (the tutorial walks through
     model serving from notebook content).
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  images, and a validation manifest.
- Validate each tutorial against the current release by executing its
  validation manifest.
- Keep each tutorial self-contained and executable end-to-end in a user
  project with no manual fix-up steps.
- The deployment and RAG tutorials exercise model-serving and LLM/RAG
  platform surfaces; those components keep working as-is — their correct
  behavior during tutorial execution is verified as part of tutorial
  validation, with no code changes to them.
- Notebook structure, dataset choices, and level of detail are content
  decisions for the delivering team.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist, one per journey listed in Scope.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format with metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest.
- Each tutorial's validation manifest executes successfully against the
  current release.
- Each tutorial launches end-to-end through the Dashboard gallery's
  workbench launch path into a user project.
- Tutorial content is reviewed for technical accuracy against current
  platform behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, partial): Six curated tutorials exist covering the core
  journeys; each is tested against the current release. This epic covers the
  five notebook-delivered journeys; the first-pipeline journey is delivered
  by the pipeline tutorial work.

# Document tutorial gallery usage and the tutorial contribution process

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for the tutorial gallery: how users
use the gallery to launch getting-started tutorials, and how teams
contribute new tutorials to the curated set. Documentation follows the Red
Hat docs content process.

## Scope

- Author a documentation topic covering using the tutorial gallery:
  finding tutorials and launching them into a project (workbench and
  pipeline launch modes).
- Author a documentation topic covering the contribution process for new
  tutorials: how a tutorial is authored, packaged per the tutorial packaging
  format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), validated, and
  accepted into the curated gallery.
- The contribution process is documented only — no submission tooling is in
  scope for this release, and tutorial content localization is out of scope,
  matching the strategy's out-of-scope statements.
- Exact topic placement and structure follow the existing documentation
  set's conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains how to use the tutorial gallery,
  accurately reflecting the shipped gallery behavior.
- Published documentation explains the contribution process for new
  tutorials, accurately reflecting the tutorial packaging format.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and
  the shipped tutorials (reviewed by the teams that built them).
- No contribution tooling or localized content is documented as available.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

## Triage

architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review
processes — product code (Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), content
authoring (the tutorials themselves), and documentation — across four
components (Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines, Documentation).
Full decomposition follows.

No Staff Engineer Input section is present in the strategy, so the
High-Level Requirements and Problem Statement are the authoritative scope.
